items.stem: What is air?
options: A mixture of different gases
Only one gas, oxygen
Only one gas, nitrogen
Empty space with nothing in it

explain.why: Air has oxygen but also nitrogen and other gases.
Nitrogen is the most plentiful gas, but it is not the only one.
Air is made of gases, which are matter.

solution: Air is a mixture of gases such as nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and water vapour.

items.stem: Which gas makes up the largest part of air?
options: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Water vapour
Nitrogen

explain.why: Oxygen is about one fifth of air, so it is second.
Carbon dioxide is only a tiny part of air.
Water vapour is a small part of air and its amount changes.

solution: About 78% of air is nitrogen.

items.stem: A candle burns in a room. Which gas in the air does the flame use?
options: Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Water vapour

explain.why: Nitrogen does not help things burn.
Carbon dioxide does not support burning.
Water vapour does not help things burn.

solution: Burning needs oxygen.

items.stem: Which gas in air do we need to stay alive?
options: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Water vapour

explain.why: We give this out when we breathe out.
We breathe nitrogen in and out, but our bodies do not use it.
Our bodies do not need water vapour from air for respiration.

solution: Living things use oxygen for respiration.

items.stem: Which gas turns limewater milky?
options: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen in the air
Nitrogen
Water vapour

explain.why: Oxygen does not change limewater.
Nitrogen does not change limewater.
Water vapour does not turn limewater milky.

solution: Carbon dioxide is the gas that makes limewater turn milky.

items.stem: A green plant is placed in bright light. Which gas does it add to the air?
options: Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Smoke
Oxygen

explain.why: Plants do not make nitrogen.
In light, plants take in carbon dioxide to make food.
Plants do not make smoke.

solution: Plants give out oxygen when they make food in light.

items.stem: Water drops form on the outside of a cold glass of ice water. Which gas in the air formed these drops?
options: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Water vapour
Carbon dioxide

explain.why: Oxygen stays as a gas on the cold glass.
Nitrogen stays as a gas on the cold glass.
Carbon dioxide does not turn into water.

solution: Water vapour in the air cools and turns into drops of water on the cold glass.

items.stem: Mira blows up a balloon. What does this show about air?
options: Air has no mass
Air takes up space
Air is a liquid
Air is always cold

explain.why: Air has mass, but a balloon does not show that.
Air is a mixture of gases.
The balloon says nothing about temperature.

solution: The balloon gets bigger as air fills it, so air takes up space.

items.stem: Which of the following lists gases that are all found in air?
options: Nitrogen, oxygen and carbon dioxide
Oxygen, iron and nitrogen
Water vapour, salt and oxygen
Carbon dioxide, sand and nitrogen

explain.why: Iron is a solid metal.
Salt is a solid.
Sand is a solid.

solution: Nitrogen, oxygen and carbon dioxide are all gases in air.

items.stem: About how much of air is oxygen?
options: About one half
About four fifths
A tiny amount, less than one hundredth
About one fifth

explain.why: Half is far too much. Nitrogen is the biggest part.
Four fifths is about the amount of nitrogen.
That is about the carbon dioxide.

solution: Oxygen is about 21%, which is about one fifth.

items.stem: The pie chart shows the gases in air. Which slice stands for nitrogen?
options: Q
R
P
None of the slices

explain.why: Q is the second biggest part, which is oxygen.
R is the smallest part.
Nitrogen is the largest part of air.

solution: Nitrogen is about 78%, the biggest slice.

items.stem: The pie chart shows the gases in air. Which slice stands for oxygen?
options: P
Q
R
P and R together

explain.why: P is the biggest slice. Oxygen is not the most plentiful gas.
R is far smaller than the amount of oxygen.
Oxygen is one gas and has one slice.

solution: Oxygen is about 21%, the second biggest slice.

items.stem: In the pie chart of gases in air, slice R is the smallest. What belongs to slice R?
options: Carbon dioxide and the other gases
Only nitrogen
Only oxygen
Nitrogen and oxygen together

explain.why: Nitrogen is the biggest part of air.
Oxygen is the second biggest part.
Those two make up almost all of air.

solution: Carbon dioxide and the remaining gases make up only a tiny part of air.

options: P
R
P and Q together
Q

explain.why: P is nitrogen, which does not support burning.
R is the small amount of other gases.
Only oxygen is needed for burning.

solution: Oxygen supports burning and is about 21% of air, the Q bar.

items.stem: Which of these gases is found in the smallest amount in air?
options: Nitrogen
Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
They are all the same amount

explain.why: Nitrogen is the largest part.
Oxygen is about one fifth of air.
The gases are in very different amounts.

solution: Carbon dioxide is only about 0.04% of air.

items.stem: Why do we need to breathe in air?
options: To get carbon dioxide for our bodies to use
To get oxygen for our bodies to use
To fill our lungs so that they stay big
To get water vapour so that we do not need to drink

explain.why: We give carbon dioxide out.
We breathe to take in oxygen, not just to fill space.
We still need to drink water.

solution: The body uses oxygen from the air for respiration.

items.stem: A cold can of drink is left on a table. Drops of water appear on its outside. Where did the water come from?
options: Water vapour in the air
Water that leaked through tiny holes in the can
Oxygen in the air that turned into water
Water that the can made from the cold

explain.why: The can is sealed. The drops come from outside.
Oxygen does not turn into water.
Cold does not make water. Water vapour cools and forms drops.

solution: Water vapour in the air touches the cold can and turns back into water.

items.stem: Two identical candles are lit and covered by jars P and Q. Which candle goes out first?
options: The one under jar Q, because it has more oxygen
Both go out at the same time because the flames are the same
The one under jar P, because there is less oxygen in it
Neither, because a candle can burn with no air

explain.why: More oxygen lets a candle burn longer.
The amount of oxygen differs.
A flame needs oxygen.

solution: The small jar has less air and so less oxygen. The flame goes out sooner, when too little oxygen is left in the small jar.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about air is true?
options: Air has no mass because we cannot see it
Air has mass and takes up space
Air does not take up space
Air is made up of only oxygen

explain.why: We cannot see air, but it has mass.
A balloon filled with air shows that air takes up space.
Air is a mixture of gases.

solution: Air is a mixture of gases, so it is matter with mass that takes up space.

items.stem: The table shows three gases in air. Which gas is oxygen?
options: Y
X
Z
X and Y

explain.why: X is the biggest part and does not keep a candle burning, so it is nitrogen.
Z is a tiny part and does not keep a candle burning, so it is carbon dioxide.
Only one gas keeps the candle burning.

solution: Only oxygen keeps a candle burning and it is about 21% of air.

items.stem: Which of the following shows that air contains water vapour?
options: A balloon gets bigger when we blow into it
A candle goes out in a closed jar
Limewater turns milky when we breathe into it
Water drops form on the outside of a cold glass

explain.why: This shows that air takes up space.
This shows that burning uses oxygen.
This shows carbon dioxide.

solution: Water vapour cools and turns back into drops on a cold surface.

items.stem: A mouse is sealed in a jar of air for a long time. Which gas in the jar goes down?
options: Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
All the gases go down equally

explain.why: The mouse does not use nitrogen.
The mouse gives out carbon dioxide, so it goes up.
Only oxygen is used by the mouse.

solution: The mouse uses up oxygen in respiration.

items.stem: Which gas does not support burning?
options: Oxygen from the air
Carbon dioxide
Air
Pure oxygen

explain.why: Oxygen is the gas that supports burning.
Air contains oxygen, so a flame can burn in it.
More oxygen makes a flame burn brighter.

solution: Carbon dioxide does not support burning.

items.stem: A student breathes out through a straw into limewater. The limewater turns milky. Which gas is in the air we breathe out?
options: Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Oxygen, which turns limewater milky
Water vapour

explain.why: Nitrogen does not change limewater.
Exhaled air still has oxygen, but oxygen does not change limewater.
Water vapour does not turn limewater milky.

solution: Limewater turns milky with carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Tube X has fresh air pumped into limewater. Tube Y has air from the lungs blown into limewater. Y turns milky faster. What does this show?
options: Fresh air has no carbon dioxide at all but air from the lungs has some
Air from the lungs has more carbon dioxide
Air from the lungs has no oxygen left in it, unlike fresh air
Limewater reacts with oxygen in the air from the lungs

explain.why: Fresh air has a very small amount.
It has less oxygen, not none.
Limewater turns milky with carbon dioxide.

solution: More carbon dioxide turns limewater milky faster.

items.stem: Which conclusion about the air we breathe in and out does the table support?
options: Exhaled air has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide than inhaled air
Air we breathe out has more oxygen than air we breathe in
Air we breathe out has no carbon dioxide
Air we breathe in has more carbon dioxide than air we breathe out

explain.why: The table shows 16% against 21%.
The table shows 4%.
The table shows 0.04% against 4%.

solution: Oxygen goes 21 to 16 and carbon dioxide goes 0.04 to 4.

The size of the jar does not change how long the candle burns for

Nitrogen does not keep a flame burning.

It goes out at once because there is no oxygen
It goes out slowly because nitrogen burns away

In air, the oxygen is what keeps the flame going.
Nitrogen does not burn.

solution: Without oxygen there is nothing for the flame to use.

Water vapour

Carbon dioxide goes up in exhaled air, but X stays the same.
Water vapour is not a large percentage like 78%.

solution: X is about 78% and does not change, so it is nitrogen.

options: Water vapour in air turns to liquid water on the cold bottle
Water from inside the bottle passes through the glass slowly
The cold bottle changes the oxygen in the air into water
The cold bottle pulls water out of the nitrogen

explain.why: Glass does not let water through.
Oxygen does not become water.
Nitrogen does not contain water.

solution: Water vapour loses heat to the bottle and condenses.

items.stem: After a candle goes out in a closed jar, limewater is poured in and shaken. It turns milky. What does this show?
options: The jar has run out of oxygen
The candle made nitrogen when it burned
The candle made carbon dioxide when it burned
The candle made water vapour when it burned

explain.why: Limewater does not test for oxygen.
Limewater does not change with nitrogen.
Water vapour does not turn limewater milky.

solution: Milky limewater means carbon dioxide is present.

items.stem: Which gas is matched correctly to what it does?
options: Nitrogen: turns limewater milky
Oxygen: needed for burning
Carbon dioxide: needed for burning
Water vapour: makes up most of the air

explain.why: This describes carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide does not support burning.
Nitrogen makes up most of the air.

solution: Oxygen supports burning.

items.stem: Which of the following is a mixture of gases?
options: The air in a classroom
Pure nitrogen in a tank
Pure oxygen in a hospital cylinder
Pure carbon dioxide in a fire extinguisher

explain.why: It is one gas only.
It is one gas only.
It is one gas only.

solution: Air contains several gases mixed together.

options: It burns less brightly because the jar has less nitrogen
It burns the same because the jar is only a single gas
It goes out because pure oxygen cannot burn
It burns more brightly because the jar has more oxygen

explain.why: Nitrogen does not matter to the flame.
More oxygen makes it brighter.
Oxygen supports burning.

solution: More oxygen means a brighter flame.

items.stem: A football is weighed before and after being pumped up with air. The reading is higher afterwards. What does this show?
options: Air is a solid
Air has no mass but takes up space
Air has mass
Only oxygen has mass

explain.why: The reading does not tell us the state.
Air takes up space and also has mass.
All the gases in air have mass.

solution: The extra reading is the mass of the added air.

About 1%
About 21%
About 99%

99% is the two bars together.

options: A burning candle and a breathing mouse
A burning candle and a melting ice cube
A green plant making food in light and a boiling kettle
A breathing mouse and a growing plant making food in light

explain.why: A melting ice cube does not use oxygen.
Neither uses up oxygen.
A plant making food in light adds oxygen.

solution: Burning and breathing both use oxygen.

items.stem: A pan of oil catches fire. A cook covers it with a fire blanket and the fire goes out. Why?

The blanket removes the nitrogen from the air
The blanket turns the oil into water
The blanket stops oxygen from reaching the fire

Nitrogen does not keep a fire going.
The blanket does not change the oil to water.

solution: No oxygen reaches the flame, so it goes out.

items.stem: Which gas in air changes the most in amount from one day to the next, for example between a dry and a rainy day?
options: Nitrogen
Oxygen
Water vapour
Carbon dioxide

explain.why: Nitrogen stays about the same.
Oxygen stays about the same.
Carbon dioxide stays very small.

solution: The amount of water vapour in air changes with the weather.

items.stem: Rina blows through the straw into the limewater for one minute. What will she see?
options: The limewater turns into a blue liquid
The limewater turns milky
The limewater stays clear because breath has no carbon dioxide
The limewater disappears

explain.why: Limewater does not turn blue.
Breath has more carbon dioxide than fresh air.
It stays in the tube.

solution: Air from the lungs has carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky.

Taking up space does not give more oxygen.

Nothing changes because plants do not respire

options: Nitrogen slowly changes into oxygen in the air
Carbon dioxide changes into oxygen in the air
Water vapour breaks down into oxygen in the air
Green plants give out oxygen in light

explain.why: Nitrogen does not change into oxygen.
Plants use carbon dioxide, but air does not change it by itself.
This does not happen in air.

solution: Plants return oxygen to the air.

items.stem: Which statement about air is correct?
options: Nitrogen is needed for burning, so it is used up by a flame
Carbon dioxide is the second most plentiful gas in air
Air is a mixture of gases and its water vapour amount can change
Oxygen makes up about half of the air

explain.why: Oxygen is the gas needed for burning.
Oxygen is second. Carbon dioxide is tiny.
It is about one fifth.

solution: Air has fixed large parts but variable water vapour.

items.stem: A student breathes in and out of a closed plastic bag for two minutes. What happens to the gases in the bag?
options: Oxygen goes up and carbon dioxide goes down
Oxygen goes down and carbon dioxide goes up
Both oxygen and carbon dioxide go down
Nitrogen goes down and oxygen goes up

explain.why: The student uses oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide.
The student gives carbon dioxide to the bag.
Nitrogen stays about the same.

solution: Respiration uses oxygen and makes carbon dioxide.

items.stem: Gas in a jar was tested before and after a candle burned in it. How does the gas after burning compare with the gas before?
options: It has less oxygen and more carbon dioxide
It has more oxygen and less carbon dioxide
It has less nitrogen and more oxygen
It has the same amount of every gas

explain.why: Burning uses oxygen and makes carbon dioxide.
Nitrogen stays about the same.
Burning changes the gases.

solution: The candle used oxygen and gave out carbon dioxide.

options: The jar now contains more oxygen than it did before
The candle made nitrogen
The limewater has reacted with the glass of the jar
Carbon dioxide was made by the candle

explain.why: Burning uses oxygen.
Limewater does not test for nitrogen.
The change is due to carbon dioxide.

solution: Milky limewater means carbon dioxide.

The plant added oxygen both in light and in the dark

The plant had no effect on oxygen

In the dark the oxygen went down.
Both lines change.

No, it also has nitrogen and some oxygen
Yes, because the splint goes out
No, it is only nitrogen

explain.why: Other gases in a mixture do not affect that test.
A flame can also go out with low oxygen.
Nitrogen does not turn limewater milky.

solution: The jar still holds the nitrogen of the original air.

items.stem: Which method shows that air we breathe out has water vapour?
options: Breathe onto a cold mirror and look for drops
Breathe into limewater and look for a milky colour
Breathe onto a burning candle
Breathe into a balloon and measure its size after

explain.why: This tests for carbon dioxide.
This does not test for water vapour.
This shows that air takes up space.

solution: Water vapour condenses on a cold mirror.

items.stem: A candle burns under a jar standing on a table. After a while the flame goes out. Why?
options: All the air in the jar has been used up
The nitrogen in the jar has been used up
The jar has too much oxygen
There was too little oxygen left in the jar to keep it burning

explain.why: Only some of the oxygen is used. The other gases stay in the jar.
Nitrogen is not used by a burning candle.
Extra oxygen makes the flame brighter.

solution: A burning candle uses oxygen. When the oxygen left is too little, the flame goes out.

The candle wax turns into water that fills the jar from below
The nitrogen in the jar is used up by the candle

Candle wax does not turn into the water in the trough.
A candle does not use nitrogen.

It is all nitrogen, as nothing else can stay in the jar
It still has some oxygen, but too little to keep the flame going

Most of the gas left is nitrogen.
Some oxygen and a little carbon dioxide are still there.

options: Jar A, because the plant takes in the oxygen
Both the same, because the plant takes no part
Jar B, because the plant adds carbon dioxide in light
Jar B, because the plant adds oxygen in light

explain.why: In bright light the plant gives out oxygen.
The plant changes the gases in the jar.
In light the plant takes in carbon dioxide.

solution: More oxygen lets the candle burn longer.

The water is too heavy for the air outside to push it any higher
The candle used up all the gases in the jar before it went out
The candle made new oxygen as it burned, which filled the space

explain.why: The amount of gas lost sets the rise.
Most of the gas in the jar remained.
A burning candle uses oxygen. It does not make it.

solution: Only some of the oxygen is used, and the rest of the gas stays in the jar.
